title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting and purpose. This page belongs to the 'Longue Marche' notes. Its job is to establish the injectivity half of the anabelian 'Hom-conjecture' (Hom(X,Y) → outer Galois-equivariant homomorphisms of fundamental groups) in a case where it can be proved with abelian, Kummer-type tools alone. The previous page reduces a statement over an arbitrary field k to a model over a field K of finite type over Q.

Corollary 3 (modern form).
- Let K be a field of finite type over Q, with algebraic closure K̄.
- Let X and Y be geometrically connected K-schemes of finite type, with X reduced.
- Suppose Y embeds in a semi-abelian variety G, i.e. an extension of an abelian variety by a torus (see the transcription corrections), or in a torsor under one.
- We have the fundamental exact sequences 1 → π1(X̄) → π1(X) → Gal(K̄/K) → 1, and likewise for Y. Grothendieck calls these the ('extérieure') extensions E_{X/K} and E_{Y/K} of E_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/K).
- Each K-morphism f : X → Y induces a homomorphism of extensions π1(f) : E_{X/K} → E_{Y/K}, well defined up to conjugation by π1(Ȳ).
- Claim: if π1(f) = π1(g) up to such conjugation, then f = g.

Stronger, 'abelian' version. It suffices that the induced homomorphisms of the abelianized extensions coincide. These are the extensions of Gal(K̄/K) by π1(X̄)^ab and π1(Ȳ)^ab. The marginal note 'Hom(π1(X̄)_ab, …)' points to the object controlling this. As the next page explains, once arithmetic-geometric hypotheses have been reduced to this point, one can drop the anabelian structure and work abelianly, but in an arithmetic context. Compared with Cor. 1 α, which used only the geometric map H1(X̄) → H1(Ȳ), the finer hypothesis is equality of the two extension homomorphisms with kernels H1(X̄, Z_ℓ) and H1(Ȳ, Z_ℓ), for all primes ℓ.

Proof (begun on the next page).
1. It suffices to show f(x) = g(x) for every x ∈ X(L), for all finite extensions L/K. Each such L is again of finite type over Q. Since char 0 and X is reduced, X is geometrically reduced, so these points are Zariski dense, and two maps to a separated Y that agree on a dense set of points of a reduced scheme are equal.
2. A rational point x gives a conjugacy class of splittings of E_{X/K}. A fortiori it gives a splitting of the abelianized extension.
3. The hypothesis implies that f(x) and g(x) give the same class of splittings of the abelianized extension of Y. Pushing forward to G, the difference f(x) − g(x) ∈ G(K) has trivial image under the Kummer map G(K) → H^1(K, T̂(G)) = lim_n H^1(K, G[n]).
4. This Kummer map is injective because G(K) has no nonzero infinitely divisible elements: ∩_n nG(K) = 0. For the abelian part this follows from Mordell–Weil–Lang–Néron, since A(K) is finitely generated over a finitely generated field. For the torus part it follows from the structure of K* for K finitely generated (valuations plus finiteness of units and roots of unity). The extension 0 → T(K) → G(K) → A(K) then gives the statement for G.
5. Hence f(x) = g(x), and so f = g.

The argument is correct and is essentially the classical Kummer-injectivity argument, i.e. the injectivity part of the section conjecture for subvarieties of (semi-)abelian varieties.
errors: The conjugation should be by an element of π1(Ȳ) (the geometric fundamental group); the page writes π1(Y), presumably a slip or a misreading.

To pass from K-points to f = g one needs density of points over finite extensions of K and separatedness of Y; both are implicit (X reduced in characteristic 0 is geometrically reduced, and Y sits inside a separated group variety).
For the torus part, G(K) is not finitely generated (K* is not), so the argument must use the absence of divisible elements rather than Mordell–Weil. This is true but is not stated on this page.
Making the abelian criterion precise requires pushing forward to the Albanese/semi-abelian quotient (H1(Ȳ) → T(G)). This is only gestured at in the illegible margin.

ideas.what: Injectivity of Hom_K(X,Y) → outer Galois-compatible homomorphisms of fundamental-group extensions when Y lies in a (semi-)abelian variety, over fields of finite type over Q
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of the anabelian Hom-conjecture / injectivity of the section map via Kummer theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore following Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings; standard in Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki, Stix
ideas.where_published: The letter to Faltings (1983, printed in Geometric Galois Actions vol. 1, 1997) discusses injectivity via Kummer/Mordell–Weil; it is unsure whether this exact corollary appears there

ideas.what: Reduction of the anabelian hypothesis to its abelianized arithmetic shadow: equality of homomorphisms of Galois extensions by H1(X̄, Z_ℓ) and H1(Ȳ, Z_ℓ) for all ℓ suffices
ideas.modern_name: Abelian Kummer / Albanese section obstruction; 'arithmetic abelian' versus 'geometric abelian' information
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Kummer theory, Albanese map; cf. Stix, 'Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups')

ideas.what: Injectivity of the Kummer map G(K) → H^1(K, T̂G) for a semi-abelian variety G over a field of finite type over Q
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the letter to Faltings

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean, correct statement of the known injectivity part of the Hom/section conjecture for targets inside semi-abelian varieties, proved via Kummer and Mordell–Weil. The explicit remark that the abelianized arithmetic extension classes already suffice is a nice formulation, but it is standard knowledge among specialists today.
transcription_corrections: 'Y se plonge dans un catégorie d'une V.A. par un torseur' should read approximately 'Y se plonge dans une extension d'une V.A. par un tore'. This means a semi-abelian variety; 'catégorie' is a misreading of 'extension' and 'torseur' of 'tore'.
'un corps K cat. de type fini sur Q' should be 'un corps K de type fini sur Q' (the 'cat.' is a stray abbreviation or misreading).
'il suffit [?] que les lois d'extensions tout court!)' is likely an insertion reading 'homomorphismes d'extensions (tout court!)': the extension homomorphisms themselves, not merely outer classes.
'conjugués par un élément de π1(Y)' is probably intended as π1(Ȳ).
Left-margin note: something like 'Hom(π1(X̄)_ab, π1(Ȳ)_ab)' or H^1 with abelian coefficients; only partly legible.
